mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real estate activity (HOUST) by more than 5% over two months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as broader economic demand softens.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when HOUST declines by more than 5% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over two months signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic activity picks up.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO increases by more than 2% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 3% over three months signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when RSAFS increases by more than 3% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and inflation (CPIAUCSL) is rising by more than 0.5% per month, the real interest rate becomes negative, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors seek higher returns in equities.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% per month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when FEDFUNDS is below 1% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% per month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% within a month, it signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.2% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% over six months signals strong economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when GDPC1 increases by more than 2% over six months.
